content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching restriction appears anywhere in the Agreement, and § 12.3 expressly confirms the point.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", and "recruit", plus review of the likely homes for such a covenant (§ 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General), found no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching restriction binding Customer. To the contrary, § 12.3 affirmatively preserves Customer's freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. This matches the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so the fallback mutual 12-month construct is unnecessary and no redline is proposed. The only related covenant, § 12.4, binds Vendor (non-compete against Customer's analytics products) and benefits our party, so it is not flagged.
